notes: Pool = 11796 Commander-legal non-land cards with colour identity subset of B/G. Lands are deliberately excluded: build_plan.json already fixes a 36-land manabase deterministically. One theme-relevant land the plan does not have: Nesting Grounds (colourless, {1},{T}: move a counter from one permanent you control to another) - it can move -1/-1 counters and is a legal include; Grim Backwoods and Lazotep Quarry are already in the plan.

Excluded by rule: the curated MASS_LAND_DENIAL list (26 names in config.py, incomplete by construction) and set codes unf/sunf/ust/ugl/unh/und/ulst. Our cards.csv marks acorn/sticker cards (e.g. 'Attempted Murder', Unfinity sticker cards) as legal_commander=legal, which is a data artifact; dropping those sets also drops the handful of genuinely legal Unfinity cards.
Game Changers surfaced and flagged (game_changer:true): Bolas's Citadel, Demonic Tutor, The One Ring, Vampiric Tutor. Bracket 3 permits at most 3 - the architect must count them; I did not pre-trim.

COMBO BRACKET TAGS DISAGREE WITH THE TWO-CARD-INFINITE TEST. Spellbook's bracketTag maps E->1 ... R->4 (config.COMBO_BRACKET_TAGS), and it tags 'Hapatra + Blowfly Infestation' (2 cards, 22,904 popularity, infinite death/ETB triggers) as bracket 1. Bracket 3 nominally allows zero two-card infinites. Two-card infinites in this pool: Hapatra+Blowfly Infestation, Hapatra+Host of the Hereafter, Blowfly Infestation+Nest of Scarabs, Blowfly Infestation+Flourishing Defenses, High Perfect Morcant+Flourishing Defenses (tagged bracket 4), plus Mikaeus the Unhallowed pairs. Count pieces, not tags.

Every combo_lines entry is status 'needs a stack scenario'. Several assume Hapatra is on the battlefield as commander; Judge's Desk A-004 is the precedent where a Spellbook line was refuted by an actual resolve-stack run.

Role coverage: 1518/11796 (12.9%) of the in-identity non-land pool carries no card_roles entry at all (global coverage is 86.3%). 36 of my 235 entries were bucketed by my own oracle-text regex and are marked role_source='derived-text'.

Archetype-critical cards with NO card_roles entry: Nest of Scarabs, Flourishing Defenses, Black Sun's Zenith, Torment of Venom. Absence of a role is not absence of the function - these were recovered by text matching, not by the role index.

Role mis-tags found: Demonic Consultation is tagged removal:sweeper (it is a library-exile tutor) and therefore sits in the sweeper bucket - ignore it there. Craterhoof Behemoth and Finale of Devastation carry no wincon role; Craterhoof reached the wincon bucket only via my derived mass-pump regex. Treat sweeper and wincon as the least trustworthy buckets.

similarity (ability-embedding cosine to Hapatra) was computed and used at 8% of ranking weight but is DROPPED from the entries: it is actively misleading for this commander - Nest of Scarabs scores -0.47 and Flourishing Defenses is also negative, because the ability embeddings encode function+card type, not '-1/-1 payoff'. Ranking is driven by oracle-text evidence (theme_score), EDHREC rank, and synergy-rule labels.

The synergy graph is a top-10 retrieval shortlist, not a fit score. Only 6 of Hapatra's 10 listed partners are inside B/G, and they skew to very recent sets (High-Society Hunter, Jerren, Moonstone Eulogist). Its rule labels ('-1/-1 + Death Trigger', 'Tokens + Sacrifice', 'Counters + Tokens') are used here as corroboration only.

theme_score is MY construct, not a repo artifact: a weighted sum of oracle-text regex flags (places -1/-1 counters 3.5, triggers-off--1/-1 2.2, proliferate 2.6, wither 2.0, infect 1.8, persist 1.6, sac outlet 1.4, drain 1.2, dies-payoff 1.2, token doubler 1.0, ...) plus +0.16 for the 'put a -1/-1 counter -> create a token' payoff class. Reproducible from cards.csv; not validated against play results.

New-set finding: Lorwyn Eclipsed (ecl) 'blight N' is a keyword action that puts N -1/-1 counters on a creature YOU control - i.e. a repeatable Hapatra snake trigger you pay for with your own toughness. 37 cards use it; in-identity examples surfaced here are Boggart Mischief, Blighted Blackthorn, Bogslither's Embrace, Gutsplitter Gang. These are recent enough that EDHREC ranks are unreliable for them.

Weakest bucket - SWEEPER (21 surfaced): genuine -1/-1-counter sweepers in B/G are scarce (Black Sun's Zenith, Massacre Wurm, Death Frenzy, Contagion Engine, Demon of Dark Schemes); Liliana's Influence and Torment of Venom exist in-identity but ranked out. Everything else is a generic wrath that also kills your snakes, and the bucket carries the Demonic Consultation mis-tag.

Weak bucket - TUTOR (21 surfaced): card_roles collapses land-fetch and true tutoring into tutor:narrow, so I filtered ramp:land cards out of the staple stream. Genuinely unrestricted tutors in-identity are thin and two surfaced ones (Demonic Tutor, Vampiric Tutor) are Game Changers. Green Sun's Zenith, Fauna Shaman, Grim Tutor, Diabolic Tutor and Imperial Seal (Game Changer) exist in-identity but ranked below the surfaced 21 - ask and I will add them.

Weak bucket - PROTECTION (21 surfaced): almost entirely generic equipment/hexproof. Deck-specific protection (Hapatra's Mark, which removes -1/-1 counters from your own creature) ranked below the staples and is NOT surfaced. RECURSION (21) is likewise generic Golgari graveyard value - virtually none of it interacts with -1/-1 counters.

31 cards appear in more than one bucket by design (e.g. Yawgmoth, Thran Physician in draw/removal/flex); 197 unique cards are surfaced across 236 entries. Bucket sizes: ramp 21, draw 23, removal 26, sweeper 21, protection 21, recursion 21, tutor 21, wincon 23, flex 59. FLEX is intentionally oversized because this archetype's engine - -1/-1 payoffs, persist bodies, sac outlets, token doublers, aristocrat drains - mostly falls outside the role taxonomy.

What the data cannot tell you: whether a card is good, price, the current metagame, how 1/1 deathtouch snakes actually trade, and whether persist/undying creatures (Putrid Goblin, Cauldron of Souls, Mikaeus) net out favourably next to Hapatra's own counters. Those are resolve-stack and coaching questions, not data questions.
